I will still run the same wheat-maize system on all 10.1 mu, because that is what fits my land, my well water, and my family labor. I do not start from zero every year. I look first at what I did last year, then I adjust a little. On my side, fertilizer is expensive, but losing yield is more painful than spending a bit extra, so I will not cut too hard. For wheat, I will put more fertilizer and more water because wheat here needs a steadier hand through winter and spring, and if the stand is weak early, it is hard to recover later. I will use improved seed for wheat, not old saved seed, because I have seen better tillering and fuller heads when people around me use good seed. For maize, I will keep hybrid seed, because around here hybrid maize is normal and the yield difference is real. I have well irrigation, so I will use that advantage instead of gambling on rain. My farm is not tiny and not very big, so I can still invest enough in seed, fertilizer, and a few sprays, but I also have to watch cash because some money must stay for pesticide, irrigation electricity, and machine work. I will keep tillage simple: rotary for wheat after maize, and mostly no-tillage for summer maize after wheat so I can plant fast and catch moisture. I do not chase fancy methods. I do what has worked on fields like mine, and I adjust a little for cost and yield.
